I'll go through each window carefully, checking for the four failure modes.

**W1**: "The moment was not quite so triumphant as it ought to have been." — "as it ought to have been" is a callback implying a prior triumphant event not established in this window. However, this is a chapter opening ("A SET BACK") and the phrase is narratively self-contained enough. The cabman scene is self-establishing. I'll let this pass as literary compression.

**W2**: Opens with the same paragraph as W1's second paragraph — no issues, self-contained.

**W14**: "told him everything—how Whittington had believed she knew about Jane Finn, how he had paid, and how she had named a time to return." — "Whittington," "Jane Finn," "he had paid," "she had named a time to return" all refer to prior events, but these are named characters and summarized backstory functioning as exposition. The window tells us what happened. Marginal, but readable.

**W22**: "That's him! That's Whittington! And the other?" — "That's him!" requires a referent for "him" not in this window. A reader sees only "That's him!" with no prior description of who "him" is pointing to. However, Whittington is immediately named, so the pronoun resolves within the sentence. Fine.

**W39**: "Two of the five-pound notes died gallantly." — "the five-pound notes" is a definite reference with no notes introduced in this window.

**W47**: "Back in the street they stared at one another." — "they" has no antecedent in this window (W47 starts with a line of dialogue "Afraid I don't. They left rather suddenly." — the "they" in the street refers to characters not established in this window).

**W48**: Same issue — "they" staring at each other has no antecedent in this window (it opens mid-scene).

**W36**: Opens with `"Off I go where?"` / `"Follow him, of course!"` — "him" has no antecedent in this window.

**W34**: "off you go" and the plan reference "put him off again" — "him" has no antecedent in this window.

**W49**: Opens with `"That's torn it"` — connective/callback to something not in the window, but this is a short dialogue response, a known limitation. However "And I never suspected it" — "it" has no antecedent.

**W25**: Opens with "After all, you know, you can't bluff him forever." — "him" has no antecedent in this window.

**W26**: Same — "him" in "you can't bluff him forever" carried from W25's first paragraph into W26, but in W26 the first paragraph contains the "him" reference without antecedent.

**W23**: "What is this going to lead to?" — "this" could dangle, but it refers to the Jane Finn business just discussed (the outlandish name). Borderline but resolvable from within the window.

**W38**: "Sort of thing one reads in books" — refers to sleuthing/following him. "He grinned" — "he" has no antecedent in this window (W38 opens with this sentence).

**W37**: Opens with `"Follow him, of course!"` — "him" has no antecedent established in this window.
